question: Which famous Rashtrakuta king built the rock-cut temple of Kailash at Ellora?
solution:
The correct answer is the **Rashtrakuta King Krishna I.**

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points:__**__Krishna I__

__
 
• He conquered the territories that were still under the Chalukyas
 
• He also occupied Konkan.
 
• Krishna I also defeated Vishnuvardhana of Vengi and the Ganga king of Mysore.
 
• He was a great patron of art and architecture.
 
• The Kailash Temple at Ellora was built by the Rashtrakuta King Krishna I.
 
• The Kailasa temple (Cave 16) is the largest of the 34 Buddhist, Jain, and Hindu cave temples and monasteries located along the sloping basalt cliff at Ellora Caves.
 
• Generally, most of the excavation was completed by Rashtrakuta king Krishna I (r. c. 756 - 773) in the eighth century, although some elements were added later. 

 [IMAGE: https://static.toiimg.com/thumb/66499582.cms?resizemode=75&width=1200&height=900] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** __Govinda III (793 - 814)__

__
 
• The Rashtrakuta king who defeated the Pratihara ruler Nagabhatta II was Govinda III
 
• Pala King Dharmapala and his protégé Charayudh sought the help of Govinda III.
 
• His kingdom spread up to the Vindhyas and Malava in the north and the river Tungabhadra to the south.
 
• Govind III's northern campaign was not for empire expansion but for fame.
 
• Govind III defeated Pratihara king Nagabhatta II in 793 - 814 AD.
 
• Govind III further defeated the Pallava king Dantivarman in 803 at Kanchi.

**Jai Chand:**

 
• King Jai Chand__ was defeated by **Muhammad Ghori **in the Battle of Chandawar.
 
• The **Battle of Chandwar** took place between **1193 and 1194 CE.**
 
• **Prithviraj Chauhan** was the king of **Chauhan dynasty**, reigns between **1178 to 1192 CE.**
 
• Bhima II was a member of the **Chaulukya or Solanki dynasty**, reigns between **1178 to 1240 CE**.
 
• Kumarpala was an Indian king from the Chaulukya or Solanki dynasty of Gujarat reigns between **1143 to 1172 CE.**
